about: RollSense's pixels pass (FR-141, NFR-022) on a Windows laptop: every photo's hash and CLIP embedding, as the app reads them (sort_pass_bench, cold then warm), with telemetry every second (CPU, clock, the pass's memory, GPU, disk, temperature) downsampled to 15 s. A load test, not the usual use: a trip is 2,000 to 3,000 photos (owner, 2026-11-20).
machine: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 8, Intel i7-10610U (4 cores, 8 threads, 15 W), 16 GB, Windows 10, mains power, High performance
set: 10,044 photos on the internal disk (9,713 readable by path; JPEG, PNG, Canon and Sony RAW), named by count only

scale.about: The M3 is not measured on this set. Two ways to scale the laptop's time disagree: the same 22 CC0 photos on 2 threads today (M3 239 ms, on battery with its swap nearly full: not a quiet machine) give 3.06; the app's 8 threads against the M3's 55 ms of 2026-11-18 (OPTIMIZATION §5) give about 9.5. The M3 is to be measured on a quiet machine before the release; the public page shows the laptop's figures only.
